players.product: balance-of-plant EPC for on-site gas turbines at AI campuses (Fermi Project Matador phase one) and behind-the-meter generation for data centers

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Dodgen: Q2 revenue was just under $1.7 billion, a decrease of about $200 million or 10.7% from the prior year, driven by the energy segment (down $236.9 million or 19.2% on decreased renewable activity, partly offset by natural gas generation, pipeline and PayneCrest for May and June); the utility segment was up $19.6 million or 2.8% on gas operations and power delivery, partly offset by lower communications revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: just under $1.7 billion Q2 revenue, down 10.7% year over year

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Dodgen: Q2 gross profit was $82.4 million, down $149.3 million; gross margin 4.9% vs 12.3% a year earlier. Utility segment gross profit $85.1 million (down $12.4 million), gross margin 11.9% vs 14.1%, on lower communications revenue and margin (fiber-to-the-home customers transitioning to BEAD programs, more maintenance work) and gas operations lacking 2025's strong project closeouts, partly offset by higher power delivery revenue and margins on substation and transmission scopes. Energy segment gross margin was slightly negative vs 10.8%, on renewables project cost overruns, partly offset by pipeline and PayneCrest.
quarterly_data.figure: 4.9% gross margin (12.3% prior year); utility 11.9%; energy slightly negative

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Koti Vadlamudi: six renewable energy projects had cost overruns; two are now complete, three are expected to reach substantial completion in Q3 2026, and the sixth is expected to reach mechanical completion in early November and substantial completion by year-end; the rest of the renewables portfolio (probably over two dozen projects) is on average performing within expectations. CEO: the renewables impact 'is not representative of the performance standards we have historically defined at Primoris, nor is it acceptable to me as CEO'; CFO: Q2 is expected to be the low point for the year.
quarterly_data.figure: six projects with cost overruns: two complete, three in Q3 2026, one by year-end

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Koti Vadlamudi: record Q2 new awards of more than $3.9 billion - approximately $1.5 billion in the utility segment and $2.4 billion in the energy segment, of which $1.4 billion natural gas power generation (all simple cycle; Texas, Missouri, Nevada). CFO Ken Dodgen: total backlog was just under $13.9 billion, up approximately $2.2 billion sequentially and a record; fixed backlog up $1.5 billion (natural gas generation, industrial, PayneCrest electrical construction services); MSA backlog up about $700 million, mainly power delivery; renewables backlog was $2 billion at the end of Q2; Q3 started with additional natural gas generation and pipeline bookings.
quarterly_data.figure: just under $13.9 billion backlog (record); more than $3.9 billion Q2 awards

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Dodgen: maintaining the June guidance for full-year 2026 - EPS of $1.30-$1.85, adjusted EPS of $2.05-$2.60 and adjusted EBITDA of $275-$325 million; adjusted EBITDA expected at $90-$110 million in Q3 and $100-$120 million in Q4, with sequential improvement in revenue and earnings; on the range: 'We're just giving ourselves plenty of room'. He expects a return to revenue growth and margin expansion in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA $275-$325 million; Q3 $90-$110 million; Q4 $100-$120 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Dodgen: energy segment gross margin expected in the 6%-8% range for full-year 2026 - Q3 'kind of in that 6%-8% range', Q4 'more kind of 8%-10%', then 'back to full 10%-12% next year' (CEO: 2027 cadence in the normal 10%-12% range); SG&A a little over 6% of revenue for 2026 with higher PayneCrest amortization; full-year effective tax rate 30%-32%; free cash flow probably $150 million-$200 million for 2026, versus a prior forecast of $350 million-$400 million, the difference essentially the renewables impact.
quarterly_data.figure: energy gross margin 6%-8% for 2026, 10%-12% in 2027; free cash flow $150 million-$200 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Koti Vadlamudi: more than $16 billion of solar and battery storage opportunities in core geographic markets; renewables backlog expected to build in H2 2026, mostly in Q4 (CFO: renewables bookings of $1.5 billion-$2 billion expected in H2, primarily Q4; CEO: one Q2 solar award 'was a couple hundred million dollars'); one signing moved from Q3 to Q4; potential for a strong Q1 2027 for renewables awards; for 2027 'modest growth ... coming off of a reset year'.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $16 billion solar and storage opportunities; $1.5 billion-$2 billion H2 2026 renewables bookings expected

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Dodgen: 'I think we're still on track' for natural gas generation revenue in the $500 million-$600 million range in 2026, and '$800 million to comfortably $1 billion in revenue next year' based on the backlog signed so far and potential other second-half signings. CEO Koti Vadlamudi on the gas generation funnel: 'I think last quarter, it was a little over $6 billion. I think now it's over $8 billion' (the CFO interjected '$7 billion-$8 billion'), then the CEO: 'It's over $8 billion that we're tracking'; the portfolio is mostly simple cycle, with a handful of combined-cycle projects in the funnel but not in backlog; Primoris checks that customers have turbine slots in the queue - 'Our relationships with those OEMs is pretty significant', and in some cases OEMs pair Primoris with a potential client; Primoris focuses on the balance of plant. Industrial revenue (including gas generation) was modestly lower year over year on timing but is on track to exceed expectations for the full year with a meaningful H2 2026 ramp.
quarterly_data.figure: $500 million-$600 million 2026 natural gas generation revenue; $800 million to comfortably $1 billion in 2027; funnel over $8 billion per the CEO (CFO interjected $7 billion-$8 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Koti Vadlamudi: most end markets are labor-resource-constrained; in natural gas generation 'the demand is outstripping supply' - about eight to nine teams today, up from half a dozen last year; in power delivery 'resources are tight', with customers of peers that are 'tapped out' seeking additional help; pipeline customers are tendering a year and a half to potentially two years in advance to secure resources.
quarterly_data.figure: eight to nine gas generation teams (from half a dozen)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Koti Vadlamudi: 'there is a strong demand environment created by AI data centers'; data center work is 'probably 10%-15% of the total portfolio' at any given time; most data-center opportunities Primoris sees 'anecdotally' are on-premise generation. Data center fiber and connectivity, including the fiber that interconnects AI data center clusters, is an important growth driver for communications.
quarterly_data.figure: data centers probably 10%-15% of the total portfolio

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Koti Vadlamudi: PayneCrest (electrical construction services, part of Primoris for two months of the quarter) delivered stronger than anticipated revenue and margins; roughly $200 million of backlog associated with the acquisition at quarter end, and PayneCrest added $250 million in bookings in the quarter on top of the acquired backlog (about $450 million of the Q2 energy awards came from PayneCrest); its relationship with one hyperscaler in particular is allowing it to capture further work, and labor resources are its gate to growth; data center exposure is not a majority of its portfolio; a 'light touch integration', with revenue synergies where Primoris uses subcontractors.
quarterly_data.figure: $250 million PayneCrest bookings in Q2; roughly $200 million acquired backlog

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Koti Vadlamudi: pipeline delivered another quarter of double-digit revenue growth with substantial margin improvement as recovery from the 2025 cyclical trough continues; the multi-year larger-diameter pipeline project funnel now exceeds $7 billion in total contract value, with upside in pipeline and natural gas generation for projects ramping in late 2027 and early 2028. Utility: power delivery demand 'is very high', customers shifting focus from distribution to transmission and substation; gas operations exceeded market revenue growth expectations, with new programs pursued in the Midwest and Southern regions; normal seasonality expected with Q3 the peak. Communications (around $400 million+ of business) is softer as fiber-to-the-home moves to BEAD-funded projects; about $300 million of BEAD pursuits tracked.
quarterly_data.figure: pipeline funnel exceeds $7 billion; communications around $400 million+; about $300 million BEAD pursuits
